Dear Oliver,

Re: Lock repair request, Flat 23, 155 Willowmere Road, Alderwick, ZZ5 2ZZ (Ref R/PM022-1).

Our records show you called the tenant, Amelia Oakley, on 18/11/2024 to say you were on your way with two locks, but we have no job report yet. Please could you let us know:
- whether you attended and what was found;
- whether the lock was repaired or replaced, or if further work or a return visit is needed;
- the cost of any work carried out or proposed (please send a quote first for anything not yet done, as it may need the landlord's approval).

Thank you,
Donna
Maintenance team, Northbridge Lettings

input.body: Hi Amelia, this is Donna from Northbridge Lettings about the front door lock at Flat 23, 155 Willowmere Road (Ref R/PM022-1). Did the contractor attend on Mon 18 Nov, and is the lock now working properly? Please reply to let us know. We've also asked the contractor for their report and will update you by Wed 20 Nov.

data.reasoning: Since the contractor arrived on 18 Nov with two locks but there's no confirmation of completed work by the 19th, I should follow up directly with the contractor for a status report, and possibly check with the tenant to confirm if the lock issue is resolved. I'll send one message to each, keeping in mind any lock replacement cost would need landlord approval that hasn't been obtained yet.

result.summary: I've asked the contractor and the tenant what happened with the lock job. The contractor, Oliver Sawyer, phoned the tenant on 18 Nov to say he was on his way with two locks. By 19 Nov there was still no report on the work (event 012). I emailed the contractor asking whether he attended, what he found, whether he repaired or replaced the lock, and what it cost. I texted the tenant to ask whether the lock now works, and put the ticket on hold until 20 Nov to chase them.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 011 shows the contractor was on his way on 18 Nov. Event 012 says there's no record of the work. The contractor and the tenant can both say what happened, so asking them is the right step before escalating. The lock is stiff but still works, so this isn't an emergency. I kept the ticket at 'scheduling' because nothing confirms the contractor actually turned up.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The missing information can come straight from the contractor or tenant. Nothing is overdue twice yet.

alternatives_considered.option: Move stage to works or closeout
